Standing reach: 8-7 1/2

Maximum vertical jump: 29.5 inches
Second round to undrafted

Scouts Inc. Old-school, undersized power forward who can score inside. Strong and tough. Wide-body who loves to post up and finish inside. Seals extremely well and can shoot the baby-hook with either hand. Simple, power-drop step inside as he is very clever at creating post-up space down low.

Not a great athlete and does not have great lift to the rim, but his strength and toughness compensate for his lack of great leaping ability. His strength and very good footwork make him a good low-post defender. Might have a tough time guarding quick, slashing, athletic perimeter players.

A capable face-up shooter from 17 feet and in. He must be played on the perimeter facing, as he is able to put it on the floor and get his own shot. Excellent hands; catches everything inside. Not capable of putting it on the floor and creating for his teammates.

Good rebounder because of his strength and toughness. The more physical it gets, the better he gets. Will not back down from anyone. Has a rebounder's mentality but not great leaping ability. A hard-hat rebounder.

Will he be able to finish inside against taller, more athletic inside players?
The Wolves get an undersized bruiser. They need his toughness, but I've never been a huge fan of the undersized power forward.

He's long (he's got a 7-foot-2 wingspan), athletic, powerful and very skilled.  Has a nose for the basketball.  Very aggressive.  Can score both inside and out.  Good rebounder.  A potential double-double guy.  His explosiveness is beginning to return now that his knee has rehabbed.

He's a little undersized for the position.  Most scouts believe he's closer to 6-foot-7.  However, his huge wingspan makes up for a lot of that, much like it did for Ike Diogu last year.  The injuries, especially the knee, worry some scouts.

Powe declared for the draft on April 19, and hired agent Aaron Goodwin, ending his college eligibility. One of the top players in the country coming out of high school.  Injured his ACL as a junior in high school and then reinjured it toward the end of his freshman year.  Missed his entire sophomore season recovering from the injury.  A stress fracture kept him off the floor for the first month of the 2005-06 season.
Late first to early second

Physicals and workouts are essential for Powe. If he can go into NBA workouts and wow teams with his athleticism and get a clean bill of health from doctors, he'll probably fall somewhere in the 20s or early 30s. If he's lost a step or team doctors are concerned about the long-term prognosis on his knees, he could slip all the way out of the draft.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Powe is a powerful inside player who has been a 20-point, 10-rebound guy throughout his career college career. He has persevered through two knee injuries and a stress fracture in the past four years.

Offensively, he is a strong, inside presence. He is not overly athletic, but he is a brute. He loves to muscle his way to the hoop and overpower his defender. In college, his favorite move was the back-down dribble into the paint. His dilemma is whether his offensive skill set will be able to work in the NBA.

Powe has exhibited very good vision on double teams in the post. He reads the doubles and has shown the ability to make the correct play. His Achilles' heel is his shooting ability and range. He looks uncomfortable when he strays out to the 17-foot range. He is not bad catching the ball at the elbow or just off the block. He does not have a lot of finesse to his game and instead tried to overpower his defender on the drive. He loves to go right. He is a high-volume free-throw shooter who got to the line 10 times per game last season.

He has a nose for the ball and a real knack for rebounding. He is an excellent offensive rebounder because he is physical and is able to move bodies for position. He is very tough to box out on the weak side, because he is good at getting into his defender's lower body and moving him out. On the defensive end, he uses his strength, lays a body on his man and boxes out.

Powe's game is not flashy or pretty, but it is very efficient. He has a "junkyard dog" type of game, along with the body and strength to play at the next level.

Powe's size is less of an issue thanks to his big wingspan.
(Larry Goren/Icon SMI)

A more athletic Ike Diogu

The Nuggets traded this pick to the Celtics. There is good value here. If he hadn't hurt his ACL twice, he'd have been a mid-first round pick. He was a double-double guy at Cal. If he stays healthy, he'll help the Celtics down the road.

Gibson has just about everything you could ask for in an offensive player. He's a smooth athlete who has good size for the position. He has the ability to score from the perimeter or by attacking the basket, and he's great in the open court. He gets to the line.  Good on-the-ball defender.

Scouts were never totally convinced that he's actually a point guard and his play this season has raised serious concerns. He still makes too many mistakes, has difficulty handling defensive pressure, over dribbles the ball and appears turnover prone.  If he is a two, then he's undersized for the position.
Late first to early second

Gibson was ranked very highly by many scouts coming into the season, but his uneven play at the point has given them pause. While there's nothing wrong with Gibson's offensive game, he continues to struggle to run a team sustaining serious questions about whether he can be a full-time point guard at the next level. He may turn into more of a scoring combo guard in the pros. Word is that he's got a promise either with Cleveland at No. 25 or the Rockets at No. 32.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Gibson was one of the top college point guards in the country last year, leading Texas deep into the NCAA tournament. The question is whether he can run a team and be a full-time point guard in the NBA. Gibson is very crafty, has good size, and is excellent in the open court. But his lack of explosiveness and length will hurt his chances at the next level. He has trouble blowing by athletic point guards and getting into the teeth of the defense.

Due to his lack of length he will also have trouble making the necessary plays, because a lot of his passes will be deflected. Longer guards will have a major advantage over him by being able to pass around or over him.

Gibson can shoot the ball to about 18 feet, but he is a streaky shooter and does not have deep range. He does have toughness and can play on the run, but he has had some issues with turnovers. As a freshman, he had as many turnovers as assists. He improved those numbers this year averaging 3.1 assists and only 1.9 turnovers. He will need to be much more consistent in his ball-handling and decision-making at the next level.

Gibson simply isn't athletic or explosive enough to be an effective scoring point guard. In addition, his decision-making is not where it needs to be yet. Gibson needs to demonstrate that he can run a team and make sound decisions in order for a NBA coach to trust him with the ball. Look for Gibson to get drafted early- or mid-second round.

Gibson's got game, but is his handle good enough for the NBA?
(Elsa/Getty Images)

Poor man's Ben Gordon?

Another great pick for the Cavs. Gibson was ranked at No. 5 in our preseason Top 100. He slid because scouts were disappointed that he wasn't a pure point guard.  But he is an excellent shooter and athlete and could be Ben Gordon-type player in the pros. The Cavs are clearly loading up in the backcourt.

Super-athletic point guard.  Excellent body.   Long wingspan. Good quickness.  Is a real point guard.  Sees the floor very well.  Good finisher around the basket.  Excellent in the up-tempo game.  Good, tenacious defender.
He's a little bit undersized for his position.  His jump shot is improving, but still needs work.  Can be a little careless with the ball.

Blalock announced that he's declaring for the 2006 NBA Draft and hired an agent, ending his college eligibility.

Wingspan: 6-6

Standing reach: 8-0 1/2

Maximum vertical jump: 40 inches
Second round

He's a sleeper. Has been working out very well in individual workouts.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Blalock was a three-year starter at point guard and the primary ball handler at Iowa State. He plays bigger than his height because of his extraordinary 6-foot-6 wingspan. He is an extremely athletic and explosive guard with a tremendous vertical leap and is outstanding on the break or in the open floor where he can utilize his speed and quickness. Blalock gets to the paint and creates for himself or others. He was as good as anybody in the country on the fast break and would be great with an up-tempo team in the NBA.

Blalock is a proven floor leader who makes others around him better. He has excellent court vision, is a great passer and always finds the open man. He led the Big 12 in assists and was 11th in the country at 6.1 per game. He needs to become more comfortable running pick-and-rolls. He has worked hard at improving this phase of his game, but like many young guards he needs to improve his instincts for reading the defense and taking what it gives you. One knock on Blalock is that he is too unselfish and disappears at times. He needs to learn in the NBA how to take over a game at crucial times and not take a back seat to lesser players.

Blalock will go as far as his jump shot will take him. He has improved his range over his time at Iowa State and has surprised several NBA teams with his shot. He has used more of a set-shot on the 3-pointer and needs to develop more of a 1-2 step and quicker release. He has a great first step and pull-up in the lane, which will serve him well in the NBA.

Although Iowa State played a lot of 2-3 zone, Blalock is a great defender with quick hands. He will be a very good on-the-ball defender against NBA point guards.

Blalock might not have the name recognition of some of the other top point guards in the draft, but many NBA people feel he is passing some of those players each day.

Nice pick for the Pistons. They needed a point guard who can defend and handle the ball, and this is a steal. Great strength and athleticism. He's a little undersized, but he's got a chance to make the Pistons' roster.
Williams has great size, athleticism, ball handling, shooting skills and versatility for the position.  Very long. He has point-forward type skills.  His strength is on the perimeter right now.

Williams' bad shot selection, questionable work ethic and the tendency to disappear for huge stretches have hurt his draft stock this season.  Needs to get stronger.  He's still very raw and probably one of the least prepared to contribute in the NBA right away.

Williams could use more polish in his game.
(Nick Laham/Getty Images)

Wingspan: 7-3

Standing reach: 8-8

Maximum vertical jump: 31 inches Announced on April 25 that he was declaring for the 2006 NBA Draft. Williams hired agent Bill McCandless, ending his college eligibility. Before his one year at Memphis, Williams averaged 30 points, 10 rebounds and 8 assists per game for Laurinburg (N.C.) Institute. The Tennessee native put up 15 points and 6 rebounds on 6-for-11 shooting at the Jordan Classic. Williams declared for the draft last spring, but withdrew after he couldn't get a first-round promise.
Mid to late first round

Scouts were impressed with his fast start in Memphis, but he's cooled off considerably since then. The tools he has are unbelievable. It's just about the polish at this point. His workouts have been a little shaky which could mean he's sleeping. He could go as high as Orlando at No. 11 or slip to the Knicks at No. 29.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: Two words come to mind when people watch Williams: Upside and potential. Early in the season, he was considered one of the nation's top perimeter talents. He slumped later in the season, and that cooled off his stock considerably.

He is a long-armed small forward with NBA 3-point range. He can spot up or come off screens and knock down shots with the best of them. Williams is a very athletic player who one day could be a very potent offensive basketball player. He has drawn comparisons to Walt Williams and Steve Smith.

However, he really needed another couple of years in college to develop fully. He needs to show he is assertive on offense and can do something besides jack up shot after shot. He needs to mature and compete on both ends of the floor. In many games, Williams disappeared for long stretches, which will scare some GMs away from taking a chance on him. Williams needs to toughen up and be patient. He's not too far away, but he needs time to get there.

While I knew the Pacers liked him, I'm a little surprised here. Physically he's the prototypical small forward. He runs the floor, handles the ball and can shoot the three. But the word on Williams is that he lacks heart and basketball smarts. He disappears in big games. And given that the team drafted Danny Granger last year, I'm not sure how Williams fits. The Pacers needed a point guard, a scoring, penetrating guard and help in the middle. There were several prospects I thought were better fits -- Marcus Williams, Shannon Brown, Olexsiy Pecherov, and Alexander Johnson.
He's long and athletic.  Armstrong is an explosive leaper with excellent shot-blocking timing.  He hustles up and down the floor and plays with a lot of enthusiasm.  Good rebounder.

Offensively he's still very raw.  Doesn't have any real moves around the basket.  He's also turnover prone, which makes the UConn guards reluctant to pass him the ball.  Consistency will be the biggest issue. Can he stay focused enough to play this hard every night?

Wingspan: 7-4

Standing reach: 9-1

Maximum vertical jump: 31.5 inches
Mid to late first round

After being virtually a non-factor for UConn the past three years, scouts were shocked to see Armstrong break out this season. His size, athleticism, rebounding and shot-blocking ability turned a lot of heads. There aren't many good centers in the draft right now ... so you never know. Could go as high as the Jazz at No. 14 or could slip to the Suns at No. 21.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Long, athletic big man with great upside. Shows the ability to score inside and can knock down the face-up jump shot from 17 feet and in. Good shot blocker and effective rebounder. Runs the floor extremely well and will finish in transition.

His post-up game is good, and he can score with a baby hook with either hand. Is very good at second and third effort on stick-backs. Needs to stay strong while posting up and not get pushed out of his post-up position.

Excellent offensive rebounder. Very active on the glass and does a good job of keeping the ball alive. His long wingspan gives him an advantage for second and third scoring chances off the offensive glass.

His basketball skills are very good for his size. He can pass, handle and shoot. He has shown steady improvement in all these areas since his career started. His upside is tremendous. Should he decide to fall in love with the game and become a gym rat, his basketball future is unlimited.

His physical and mental toughness has to continue to get better. He needs to show a little more nastiness to his game. When he figures that out, watch out. All the talent, athletic ability and ball skills to become a great one.

High character kid and low maintenance. Late bloomer with best days ahead.

The Hornets need a center in the worst way. It remains to be seen whether Armstrong was the right pick. He was very spotty in Connecticut. When he was good, he was pretty good. When he wasn't on, it was ugly. He has great size and good athleticism, but I'm not sure he's tough enough to play for Byron Scott. We're off to a 9-for-12 start in our Mock Draft version 5.3.

Big-time athlete with a freakish 7-foot-8 wingspan.  Aggressive defender who can dominate on the boards and by blocking shots.  Good agility.  Great in the open floor.  Has added some much needed strength to his body since we saw him last spring at the Reebok Eurocamp.

Still very raw offensively.  Most of his points come from dunks and offensive rebounds.  Relatively inexperienced -- he only began playing basketball three years ago.  Needs to continue to hit the weights.
Plays for Verviers-Pepinster in Belgium.  Had a dominant performance in the 2006 Hoops Summit game, scoring 15 points, grabbing 6 boards and blocking 9 shots.
Mid to late first round

Scouts were buzzing about him after his performance in the Hoop Summit. The draft doesn't have a ton of bigs and Sene has the type of upside teams look for in a big man. Could be a sleeper. Could go as high as Utah at No. 14 or Phoenix at No. 21.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: Sene is a young, athletic, shot-blocking big man. He doesn't have a feel for the game at this stage but has shown a lot of improvement over the past year. Sene needs to improve his body and his offensive game. Right now he is active on both ends of the floor and plays hard.

He can control the game at times on the defensive end. He made a big splash in the Nike-sponsored Hoop Summit in April. Like a lot of young African-born players, though, Sene has a limited feel for the game on the offensive end. He is very raw and scores most of his points in transition and off offensive rebounds.

Whatever team drafts him must put a lot of time into his development. He could make great use of the NBDL for the first year. With the lack of quality big men in this draft, Sene could be the beneficiary. He has a big upside, and if he gets with the right team and gets the correct tutelage, he could have a nice career.

We heard this pick several days ago and it took us a little while to get comfortable with the idea of Sene going this high in the draft. The Sonics have taken two raw centers the last two years -- Robert Swift and Johan Petro. I think there is a real possibility that the Sonics move this pick. The Suns and Jazz have both been hot on the trail of Sene. Let's see what develops. Seems like every pick is up for trade at this point.

analysis.text: One of the most athletic players in the country.  He can jump out of the gym. An excellent perimeter defender.  Possesses great quickness.  Is an underrated ball handler.

He's never been much of a shooter or scorer, though that's changed a little bit this season.   He still needs to add bulk to his frame.  In the past he's been reluctant to put the ball on the floor and attack the basket to avoid contact.  However, this year he's improved that area significantly.
Former McDonald's All-America.  Began his career at Florida before transferring to Cincinnati.  Declared for the 2005 NBA draft but withdrew after not getting a first-round guarantee.
Late first to early second

NBA scouts always have a fondness for great athletes with excellent pedigrees. His workouts have been strong, which could get him some consideration in the first. Right now, however, the second round is more realistic.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: A freak athlete who can run and jump with the best, White makes spectacular athletic plays with his ability to catch any lobs at the basket. He is very good in transition, as his speed enables him to get out and finish.

He is a streaky shooter and will need to improve his outside shot. Better shooter off the bounce than off the catch. When he goes off the dribble and pulls up for his jumper, he rises above everyone with his crazy jumping ability.

His passing and ball-handling ability need improvement. His decision-making is not always good, as he will make careless passes at times. He seems to have a lack of concentration at times and will try to make high-risk plays instead of fundamentally sound plays.

Should his basketball skills catch up to his athletic skills, he will be a very good player in the league. His college success was based more on his athletic ability, as he was just better at running and jumping than the people he faced.

Could be steal in the draft. Will not find a better run-and-jump player. Should his basketball skills get better, watch out.

The Blazers are sending White to the Pacers for two future second-rounders. He's one of the best athletes in the draft. He can get to the basket and he's an excellent perimeter defender. Still, I'm not sure about this draft for the Pacers. They got two great athletes, but I'm not sure they actually got basketball players.

A bit of a tweener.  Played power forward in college but doesn't have the strength to do it in the pros.  Lack of a perimeter game hurts his transition to the three.

Second round to undrafted

Strong showing at the Orlando predraft camp helped his stock. Reminds some scouts of a poor man's Darius Miles.  That's not really anything to get excited about, but means he's got a shot at the second round.

Renaldo Balkman? He plays with great energy and is a great athlete, but he averaged fewer than 10 points per game at South Carolina. No other team would've taken him in the first round. He has no skills other than running the floor -- think of a poor man's Darius Miles. He would've been a decent second round pick -- a guy who might have made a roster. Wow.

Johnson is an interesting prospect that will be
watched closely by scouts. He's got the body,
toughness, skills and athleticism to be an excellent
NBA four. Scouts say Johnson possesses a 40-inch vertical which
is pretty amazing for a big guy.  He's also shown
great speed for a big guy ever since he shed 25 pounds
last summer. Despite the weight loss, Johnson remains one of the
toughest power forwards in the draft.  He uses his
body well to gain position in the post and has a soft
touch around the basket.  He also possesses a nice jumper with range all the way to the college 3-point line.

Scouts question his size (he stands about 6-foot-9 in
shoes) in part because he possesses just an average
wingspan.  But his explosiveness off the floor makes
up for some of that.  Other scouts wonder if he'll
continue to keep himself in shape after making the
NBA.  His weight loss dramatically
improved his game.  Can he keep it off?  The fact that
he turned 23 in February also works against him.
Johnson delcared for the 2006 NBA Draft on April 13.  Johnson hired agent Jason Levian, ending his college eligibility.
Mid to late first round

Could Johnson be a first-round pick come draft night? His workouts in Orlando wowed scouts. He's also getting great feedback from NBA teams in individual workouts. There's always a need for athletic, physical fours with good offensive tools. A sleeper. Could go as high as the Bulls at No. 16, the Nets at No. 22, the Mavs at No. 28 or the Rockets at No. 32.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Johnson is one of the more underrated power forwards in this year's draft. He has the body, skill and toughness to play the position at the next level. Although Tyrus Thomas and LaMarcus Aldridge have received most of the hype, scouts covet Johnson. Don't be shocked if gets picked a lot earlier than some of the bigger names.

A rugged and strong power forward with excellent hands, Johnson can bump you in the post as well as face up and score from 12-15 feet. He has long arms and is extremely competitive on the block. Think of a less-polished Rasheed Wallace. Although we did not see this at Florida State this year, Johnson has a jump shot with range out to the college 3-point line. The ability to stretch defenses and run pick-and-pops will make him more desirable.

Johnson battled some weight issues early in his career, which slowed down his development, but he trimmed down about 25 pounds. The weight loss really helped his ability to run the floor. Johnson established himself as one of the ACC's top big men this past season and should be drafted in the first round, somewhere in the late teens to mid 20s.
A poor man's Kenyon Martin

Indiana sent this pick to Portland, which then sent it on to Memphis. Jerry West strikes again! The Grizzlies were seriously considering Johnson at No. 24 and he's a steal here. He is a great athlete for his position and is basically a poor man's Kenyon Martin. I really love the Grizzlies' draft night.

Barea is a super quick point guard with the ability to score in bunches.  He also has good handle and good court vision when he chooses to include him teammates in the game. He dished out a record 41 assists in three games at Portsmouth. He handed out 18 in the final game Saturday. To make things even sweeter, Barea had just five turnovers in the tournament. His 3-point shot still wasn't falling with any regularity, but scouts said they were impressed with his quickness and his ability to penetrate.

Given his size, the obligatory Earl Boykins comparisons come up in conversations about Barea -- the little guy who can't shoot the 3. But maybe Brevin Knight is a better comparison -- the little guy who can't shoot but who can dish out assists in high volumes.

Barea has been on the NBA's radar screen for years, but his lack of size combined with his high turnover rate and poor shooting percentage cost him the buzz he probably deserves. Still it's tough to ignore that Barea averaged nearly five turnovers per game and shot 29 percent from 3-point range against mediocre competition in college.
Barea had an awesome Portsmouth camp that really improved his draft stock. Barea has averaged 20 or more points a game for three seasons and added 8.4 apg this year.
Second round to undrafted

Barea's lack of size, especially when combined with a lack of a jump shot, limits his draft stock. But as a second-round prospect, Barea's looking pretty good. If he can repeat his performance in Orlando, he could move up into the high to mid second round.

Ager is a very good shooter with NBA 3-point range.  He can shoot both off the dribble and off the catch. He's a fantastic athlete with great quickness and hops.  He can be both an explosive driver and finisher. To top it off, he's a great kid and a hard worker.

He's a little undersized to play the two in the NBA.  Scouts believe he's closer to 6-foot-4, though a long wingspan will make up for some of that. Still needs to work on his ball handling and defensive effort.

Shooting is the name of Ager's game.
(Ronald Martinez/Getty Images)



Wingspan: 6-7 3/4

Standing reach: 8-5 1/2

Maximum vertical jump: 35 inches
Late first to early second

He was considered a marginal NBA prospect after just a so-so junior year at Michigan State, but he really shined in this season's opening tourney. He's been up and down since then. When his shot is falling he looks like a potential lottery pick. When it isn't, the rest of his game seems to come apart too. Could go as high as Phoenix at No. 27 or the Knicks at No. 29.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: Ager is one of the top wing players in this year's draft. He is an explosive perimeter guy who can slash to the basket, and he also is one of the better deep-range NBA 3-point shooters in this year's draft. That combination makes him one of the more complete offensive wings available.

He knows how to play off his defender and can score coming off screens. He will score on kick-outs and spot-ups, and he can run and score in pick-and-roll situations. What makes him such a valuable player is his ability to handle the basketball. He can play both guard positions and this will give his team many options on offense.

With his length and athleticism, Ager is a very good rebounding two-guard, which separates him from many in his position. Ager may be a little small for the shooting guard position, but his versatility to make shots and also be a secondary ball-handler will allow teams to use him in multiple positions.

His stock has fallen in some people's eyes, but don't be surprised if he is taken between picks 15 and 20.

We've had Ager pegged to the Mavs for almost a month. He has a great combination of athleticism and shooting ability. If he were a few inches taller and were to improve his handle, he would have gone much higher. Nice pick late for the Mavs.

Diaz is, hands down, one of the most athletic guards to eye the draft in quite a while.  Very fast.  Last season, he proved that he's more than just a great dunker. His outside shot and his decision-making skills have improved. No one questions his heart. Diaz is a fierce competitor whose toughness on the court has made Heat president/coach Pat Riley a fan.

What position does he play?  Size-wise, he's a point guard, but scouts aren't convinced he has the skills to play the point full time in the pros. He's raw.  Doesn't have the basketball experience of most prospects. He still plays out of control and tries to do too much.

Diaz has declared for the 2006 NBA draft and has hired an agent, Jason Levian, ending his college eligibility. Was a volleyball star before switching to basketball his senior season of high school. Named Most Valuable Player and Best Server at the 2003 Under-18 World Volleyball Championship in Thailand. Rumored to have a 50-inch vertical jump, but it's been measured to be just 41 inches at Miami.
Late first to early second

He's a guy who could see his stock really rise in individual workouts. With the success of combo guards such as Dwyane Wade, Gilbert Arenas and Ben Gordon, teams are going to give him a long look. So far his reviews have been very positive. Called the Puerto Rican Steve Francis by one GM. Could go as high as the Kings at No. 19 or the Lakers at No. 26.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: Diaz is an early-entrant who hired an agent, so there is no turning back. He is not a finished product, but he is a scorer with a wealth of talent. Although he is not a true point guard, that will probably be his position at the next level.

Diaz is a very explosive scorer, both on deep shots and off the dribble. He is a tough guy to cover. With his strong body and athleticism, he might be able to be a post-up point guard, as well. Most of his offense at Miami was created with the ball in his hands. His best NBA skill will be using pick-and-rolls.

Diaz's decision-making is worrisome for a guy projected to play point guard in the NBA. His shot selection is wild at times, but hopefully he will improve that with time and teaching. Diaz will need either to sit on someone's bench and learn or get minutes in the NBDL. He has too much talent not to make the league and should be taken late in the first round.

Love this pick for the Clippers down the road. Diaz is an elite athlete, can shoot it and is improving his handle. He could've gone in the first round, so this is great value for the Clippers. Don't be surprised if the Heat try to pry this pick away from L.A.

analysis.text: Scouts like a lot about his game.  An excellent shooter with deep range. He's quick, athletic, can create his own shot and is shooting a respectable 40 percent from three.  That's a pretty complete package for a guard.

However, that's only half the story.  Douby measures in at 6-foot-3, doesn't have many point guard skills to speak of and has a rep of being selfish on offense.  His slight build and lack of strength also work against him.
Douby declared for the 2006 NBA Draft on April 11.  Douby hired agent Keith Glass, ending his college eligibility.
Late first to early second

Douby got a lot of love in the press after several dominating offensive performances in February. A 41-point effort (and nine 3-pointers) versus Syracuse on Feb. 1 really started the draft Douby campaign. Now that he's decided to enter the draft, where will he go? NBA teams do like scorers like Douby who can come off the bench and put up some instant offense -- but only if they understand and accept their role. Can Douby? He's a bubble first rounder at this point. He could go as high as Indiana at No. 17 or slip down to a team like Houston at No. 32.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: Douby could be the steal of the draft. This kid can score. He has great range on his jump shot and has shown the ability to make shots beyond the NBA arc. He is very good at putting it on the floor and shooting one-handed floaters and mid-range shots. Does not really take it to the rim and finish.

Has long arms and is wiry strong. Good speed and quickness. He can put it on the floor and get his own shot. He has a scorer's mentality and thinks he can make any shot. Great self-confidence and wants to take big shots. Makes them in crunch time. Gets his shot off quickly and will be very good in a two-man game situation. Comes off screens intelligently and comes off thinking score. Never hesitates, which makes him such a great scorer.

He is long and athletic enough to defend, but he needs to have the same passion on defense as he does on offense. Should he get that, he will be able to guard people in the NBA.

Tough-minded kid, likes to be challenged and likes to take over the game. Has a "bring it on" attitude and loves to show people he can play. This attitude is what makes him good and is something you can't teach. Could be a big-time scorer at the next level. Super confident and has a scorer's cockiness that many players wish they had.
Poor man's Ben Gordon

Here's a pretty big surprise. The Kings have missed Bobby Jackson and needed a guy who can shoot and penetrate. But given that they drafted Kevin Martin and Francisco Garcia the last two years, I'm surprised that Douby is the guy. He's not a point guard so he's not going to back up Mike Bibby. I thought they'd go big with a player like Alexander Johnson or a guy who can play the point full-time like Rajon Rondo.

Halperin is a combo guard who can, at 6-foot-5, play both the one and the two. He's an excellent passer and decision maker who patiently probes the defense looking for the open man. He's a very good jump shooter with NBA 3-point range, but really makes his living on the mid-range jumper.  Very unselfish.  Intelligent.  Sees the floor well.  Good size for his position. Tough.
Still a little more of a two than a one.  Athleticism is a question mark for his position.  Almost a little too conservative at times.  Doesn't really take over games.  More of a role player.
Israeli guard is playing for Union Olimpija in Slovenia this season.  Averaged 13.9 ppg, 3.5 apg, 46 percent shooting in the Euroleague.
Late first to early second

Halperin is drawing rave reviews from international scouts. They love his decision-making skills, shooting stroke and athleticism. We said earlier in the year that he might be a second-round pick. After a strong Euroleague performance this season he's now getting some consideration as a candidate for the late first round. More likely, he'll go somewhere in the second to team like the Hawks (No. 33), Cavs (No. 42), Pacers (No. 45) or Wizards (No. 48).
Beno Udrih

Nice pick for the Sonics. Halperin can play both the one and the two. He impressed people at the Reebok Eurocamp with his decision-making and shooting. He wants to come to the NBA now, so the Sonics could end up with him on their roster this year.

analysis.text: Unlike other big point guards, Collins isn't just a combo guard with a few passing skills. He can handle the ball, set up the offense, make the spectacular play and score when his team needs him.  Great size and strength for the position.
He struggles shooting the ball from everywhere on the floor. He has trouble defensively against small, quick point guards.  Isn't a great NBA athlete.

Wingspan: 6-10

Standing reach: 8-7

Maximum vertical jump: 37.5 inches
Late first to early second

His stock has been really up and down. He started the season as a potential lottery pick, fell all the way to the second round mid season with poor play, came on late and boosted his stock only to watch it slide again as teams come away unimpressed in workouts. His lack of shot and athleticism are trumping his great size and basketball IQ right now. Could still go as high as Chicago at No. 16, but could slide all the way to Cavs at No. 25 or the Lakers at No. 26.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Versatile combo guard who brings several qualities to the table. Fully capable of directing a half-court offense but also can push it and make plays in an up-tempo transition game. His decision-making and understanding of valuing the ball and not turning it over is excellent. This has been instilled in him by playing in the Temple program.

Better shooter off the bounce than off the catch. Average 3-point shooter who will have to work on his NBA range. Needs to improve his outside shot. He is a streaky shooter who has to become more consistent. Can get to the rim and finish with either hand. Can pull up and be effective scoring in the in-between game. His size gives him the ability to score over smaller guards.

Excellent isolation player with the ability to go one-on-one and create his own scoring opportunity. Strong crossover move and excellent change-of-pace game He has a big-time dribble pull-back move which helps him create shots for himself. Sneaky quick and with good speed, he can beat you off the bounce and create for his teammates.

Has the ability to become a big-time defensive stopper. Leader in steals for his team and conference. Great off the ball anticipation for steals and reads passing lanes extremely well for steals. Can be a shutdown on-the-ball defender. Long arms and wiry strength. Solid combination guard who can score, defend and run an up-tempo or half court offense.
Mardy Collins? He doesn't have a position, is a below average NBA athlete, and he can't shoot. And he's the Knicks' sixth combo guard. Let's just get it over with -- Isiah's getting an "F."

Vinicius has the skills to be an NBA player.  He's a long, athletic small forward with a great jump shot. Has a scorer's mentality. He has good ball-handling skills. His handle has improved to the point that he's currently playing point guard full time for his team in Brazil. Very good in the open court.  Strong, physical defender.   Has improved his strength dramatically over the course of the year.
His shot can be streaky, and his decision making with the basketball is questionable at times.  Not an explosive leaper.   Needs more experience at a high level.  Could be a bit of a project.

Nickname is "Marquinos." Plays for São Carlos in Brazil.  Averaged 19.5 ppg and 4.5 apg in 35 mpg this season. His agent, Michael Coyne, hired Bob Donewald (a former Cavs and Hornets assistant coach under Paul Silas) to oversee Vinicius' training and coaching in Brazil. Donewald has Vinicius lifting every day and is teaching him pro offensive and defensive sets in an effort to prepare him for the NBA. Vinicius declared for the 2005 NBA draft but withdrew his name after not getting a first-round guarantee.
Late first to early second

He drew a lot of praise from the Hornets after a workout in New Orleans and could go as high at No. 15. The Bulls at No. 16, the Knicks at No. 20, the Suns at No. 21, the Lakers at No. 26 and the Mavs at No. 28 are all options as well. I don't see him slipping out of the first round.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Vinicius has a huge upside. He came on the basketball scene three years ago at the first Reebok Eurocamp in Treviso, Italy. He is long, athletic and has NBA skills. His game is very similar to that of DerMarr Johnson of the Denver Nuggets. He can score in bunches, and with his length, he can get into the lane and get his shot without any problem. He has a very good jump shot. In addition, he is very difficult to stop in the open floor with his quickness and outstanding ball-handling skills.

Some NBA teams have questioned his strength and toughness. But Vinicius has made great strides with his body, putting on 30 pounds of muscle over the past year, and it has helped his ability to finish. He also has defensive shortcomings that he must improve on to play at the NBA level.

We've known for a while that the Hornets were very high on de Souza. There was talk about taking him at No. 15, so the Hornets are thrilled to get him here. He's a skilled small forward who can shoot and handle the ball. He's still very raw, however, so don't expect anything right away.

Strong, physical and very athletic. Plays with tremendous energy and intensity. An above average leaper.  Long wing span allows him to play taller than he really is. Excellent rebounder for his size.  Tough, especially in the paint.  Good handle allows him to take him man off the dribble.  Draws a lot of fouls.
He's very undersized for his ideal position, power forward.  Even playing small forward at 6-foot-5 is a stretch.  He's a poor shooter which really limits what he can do on the perimeter.
Announced on April 24 that he was declaring for the 2006 NBA draft, and hired an agent, ending his college eligibility.
Late first to early second

Tucker is one of the toughest players in the draft to project. His lack of a position at the next level because of his combo of size and skills is a problem. Yet, when you watch him play for Texas, you wonder if he might just be a better basketball player than his teammates LaMarcus Aldridge and Daniel Gibson. I've heard a few scouts say he might just be a poor man's Charles Barkley. If scouts agree, then maybe he does have a shot at the first round.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: An early entrant, Tucker is a long, strong and rugged small forward. He is a tenacious player at both ends of the floor whom many feel plays harder than anyone in the country. In addition, he has a good basketball IQ.

Tucker made his mark and impressed people in college with his rebounding and scoring ability. He averaged 16.1 ppg this season, and his rebounding numbers increased every year at Texas. He went from 6.8 rpg in his freshman year to 9.5 as a junior. Tucker can handle the ball fairly well for his size and can take his man off the dribble and get to the free-throw line.

His biggest problem is that he struggles shooting the basketball. He has a hitch in his shot and cannot hit consistently from beyond 12 feet. This limitation will severely affect his offensive game at the next level. Tucker shot almost 75 percent from the foul line, so he is not a total non-shooter. He might be able to post up shooting guards at the NBA level because of his body, but even though he is tough and plays hard, he will have a tough time finding a position to guard in the NBA.

Tucker essentially is an undersized power forward, and thus lacks a true position. His game recalls that of Andre Emmett out of Texas Tech. Both were strong, tough, post-up wing players who struggle to shoot the basketball. Look for Tucker to be selected in the mid- to late-second round.

This is a good value pick for the Raptors. Some NBA GMs had him in the first round and have said he's a poor man's Charles Barkley. However, I'm not sure about the fit.  Joey Graham is another rough-and-tumble combo forward but has three inches on Tucker.

analysis.text: Freeland reminds me a lot of the Knicks' David Lee. He's actually a little taller and a little longer but plays with the same energy and athleticism. He flies up and down the court and has excellent hops. He's very active defensively and has great shot-blocking timing. Offensively he has skills. He's got a nice 12-foot jumper and in drills, was even sinking the international three, though not consistently. He's got a pretty good handle and will put the ball on the floor and take his man off the dribble. He gets great elevation on his jump shot, though the form still needs a little work.

Very inexperienced.  The league he was playing in is a very far behind the NBA.  Has only played high level organized ball for one year. Needs to polish his perimeter game.  His jump shot is OK, but could be more consistent.  Needs to add strength to play in the post.

Freeland's name wasn't even on the NBA's early entry list when it was released a few weeks ago. Apparently Freeland applied after the deadline, but was able to show the NBA that he intended to apply in time, so they granted an exception to his agent, Arn Tellem. Not sure exactly what that means, but that's the NBA's story. Played in the Spanish "B" league this year for Gran Canaria. He averaged 14.8 ppg and 7.8 rpg in 26 mpg this season.  Freeland has only played basketball for three years and only organized basketball at a high level for one season.  That's amazing considering how talented he looked.
Late first to early second

Who says there aren't any secrets in scouting anymore? Freeland is definitely the sleeper of the Reebok Eurocamp -- maybe of the draft. A team is going to draft him for the motor, defense and athleticism. Does he have a promise? Speculation centers on three teams: the Clippers, Timberwolves and the Blazers. The Clipps have two first-round picks and have been listening closely to their international scout Fabricio Besnati the past few years. The Wolves also have two first-round picks and Reebok Eurocamp director Pete Philo also happens to be on the staff. The Blazers have picks No. 30 and No. 31 and are also said to be fans. While most of the talk centers on him in the second round, I wouldn't be shocked to see him slip into the late first. A team could draft him and leave him overseas for a year or two to develop. A little more muscle and a little more polish and he could be a big prospect.
David Lee

Just missed this one. I had Freeland here on Monday. He came out of nowhere. He was bagging groceries for a living three years ago. He's played competitive basketball just one year. He never watched an NBA game until this year. He reminds me of a taller version of David Lee. He'll stay in Europe for a couple of years and then we'll see if he develops.

For a guy one scout called a poor man's J.J. Redick, he sure looks as though he could be more.  For starters, he shot at a better clip from 3 than Redick (43 percent compared with 42 percent).   He's also a much better rebounder than Redick, keeps his turnovers down and, although he doesn't look it, is a more explosive athlete.  Can get up and dunk it on people  Very tough.

He's undersized to play the two and his lack of lateral quickness is going to hurt him defensively in the NBA.  Can he create his own shot?  Lacks the speed to take his opponents off the dribble and struggles shooting the ball off the dribble.
Late first to early second

Gansey doesn't look anything like an NBA player. But scouts are having a hard time ignoring what he did last season. He hasn't had the hype Redick has had this season, but a couple of scouts have whispered that he might be a better NBA prospect. He's still a second-round prospect at this point, but the buzz is growing.

Scouts Inc. evaluation:Tough, hard-nosed kid who can shoot it from NBA 3-point range. Deceptive speed and quickness allows him to get out in transition and spot up and make shots. Better shooter off the catch than off the dribble.

High basketball IQ and really knows how to read and come off screens. Gets his footwork done early off of screens and has a very quick release when he comes off the screen.

Not great at breaking people down off the dribble or making players around him better, but good enough to get his own shot by effective use of the jab series. His shot fake, one dribble, shot is very good. Rarely puts it on the floor to finish at the rim. Needs improvement in this area to avoid being a one-dimensional player.

Smart enough to space and guard people on the perimeter. His speed, quickness and mental toughness are good enough that he will not be a defensive liability. Has good instincts to get to loose balls and is an adequate rebounder for his size.

A basketball junkie who loves to be in the gym and is constantly working to improve his game. With the right team, he could be a serviceable backup combo guard and be in the league and in the rotation.

Brown is one of the fastest guards in the country end to end.  Quickness allows him to penetrate and get to the basket.  Brown knows how to score and can do it in a hurry.  Proved he can play the point this year. Plays with a lot of heart.  NBA ready.  Good, NBA body.  Good pressure defender. Tough.

Is he really a point guard?  Scouts have questioned it for years. He did a lot to answer it this season, but teams still have questions. He seems more comfortable scoring the ball. A little undersized.  Has a rep as a good shooter, but didn't show it this year.
Declared for the 2005 NBA draft but withdrew after breaking his foot at the Chicago predraft camp.
Late first to early second

Brown kept saying last season that once teammates Deron Williams and Luther Head went off to the NBA, he'd finally get to play his natural position, point guard, and prove to NBA scouts that he has the skills to be more than a big-time scorer at the next level. The experiment didn't really go according to plan. Brown put up career highs in scoring and assists but also shot a shockingly low 36 percent from the field. The early reviews from workouts have been very positive. Given the dearth of good point guards in the draft, he could be on the rise.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: Brown is a winner. He is a leader and a born competitor. He was one of the top point guards in college this year, almost single-handedly carrying Illinois to a No. 17 ranking.

As a senior, Brown was the opponent's main focus every night and saw a lot of double-teams. Brown is very quick with the ball in his hands, has a high basketball IQ and makes good decisions. He has deep shooting range that extends to the NBA 3-point line.

Brown's height will be an issue with some teams. Earl Boykins and Jameer Nelson are both small, but they change the game with their athleticism and explosiveness. Brown doesn't posses the same natural ability, but he has heart, a brain and is a proven winner.

With most of the point guards in this year's draft lacking maturity, shooting and other traits, Brown could be the answer for a team that needs a tough and gritty floor general. Brown may stick with a team as a back-up point guard or could one day be a spot starter.
A bigger version of Earl Boykins

Great pick for the Jazz. As a speedy backup point guard, Brown is a change of pace from former college teammate Deron Williams. He plays pesky defense and can really score when you let him go. He could be an Earl Boykins-type player. The Jazz are on a roll tonight.

Boone has all the tools to be a great power forward in the pros.  He runs the floor, blocks shots, rebounds on both ends of the floor, plays the game with great energy and is starting to figure out how to finish around the basket on the offensive end of the floor.  Teams feel like he is long enough to play center on a running team, but better suited as a power forward in a more traditional half-court offense.

Does Boone really like to play?  Some at UConn wonder whether he has the drive, both on and off the court, to ever become a great player. After a stellar start to his sophomore season, he's had a number of truly awful performances for UConn that really make you wonder.

Boone got off to a great start last season, averaging 17.5 ppg, 11.3 rpg and 3.7 bpg before hitting the wall in January.  An injury in the USA Basketball trials kept him out of the competition this summer.
Late first to early second

Another shaky season makes you wonder about his NBA future. Scouts love his size, athleticism and rebounding skills, but it looks like he's still struggling to find any sort of consistency. May still be a first rounder because of his size, but his play hasn't warranted such a high selection. He's testing the draft waters this spring, but I'm not sure he's going to like the temperature.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Boone is a player who reeks of potential. His height, length and athleticism make him a player. He can run the floor extremely well for a big man and is an excellent rebounder and shot-blocker. He has been very well coached and was a defensive presence for Jim Calhoun and UConn Huskies. However the more you watch him, the more you wonder if he is mentally soft. He disappears in games and has a very limited feel offensively. In addition, Boone has a strength issue. He needs to bulk up or he will get pushed around and worn down at the NBA level.

The question all scouts have about Boone is: What is his game? He is not a shooter, scorer or one-on-one player. He has no true offensive game at this point in his career. He cannot score one-on-one on the low box, stepping away from the hoop, or by putting the ball on the floor. He only finishes around the hoop on offensive rebounds and garbage. No NBA team would be calling a play for him.

Boone scored 12.4 ppg as a sophomore, but his numbers dropped with the emergence of Hilton Armstrong this past season. While rotating in and out of the lineup this year, Boone scored only 10.3 ppg. In addition, his rebounding numbers dropped from 8.4 per game as a sophomore to 7.0 as a junior.

If Boone, a former Big East Defensive Player of the Year, is going to make the NBA, it will be because of his defense, rebounding and shot-blocking. He is a classic example of an underclassman who is confused about whether to stay in the draft or go back to college. There are one or two teams that would take a chance on him late in the first round or early in the second because of his potential.
A poor man's Drew Gooden

I'm not a huge fan of Josh Boone. However, he does have the skills the Nets want.  He runs the floor, is active on the boards and blocks shots. But does he have the heart to help the Nets? That's the big question. His workouts were horrible, with numerous scouts saying he didn't really compete. If his attitude changes, he'll be a good pick. If it doesn't, I think the Nets made a big mistake passing on Alexander Johnson here.

Second round

He's not an easy guy to peg as far as draft stock goes. Some scouts really like his game and think he could sneak into the late first round. Others aren't excited at all and think he'll be lucky to be drafted in the second round. His play in the Orlando predraft camp could be key. If he's good there, ala David Lee last year, he'll move up.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: One of the top big men in the Big Ten last year, Augustine has great length and possesses NBA skills. He is a big man who can run, shoot and mix it up. Augustine is a very strong kid who is able to face up his defenders or take them down low and be physical in the post. He has good perimeter skills and handles the ball very well for a big man.

Augustine has very good hands and can score going over either shoulder in the post. He has good footwork on his post moves and possesses enough tricks in his game to get the job done. However, at the next level he will not be a go-to type guy. Although Augustine does not possess 3-point range, he can step out and shoot from 18 feet, which will make him a serviceable pick-and-pop power forward in the NBA. He needs to add some strength so that he can handle the bumping and grinding, however.

Augustine might not be drafted very high, but he could be one of those guys who will stick on a roster and have a solid pro career. He is a skilled big man without all the flash. He might be a poor-man's version of Jeff Foster, with a better jump shot. He will be a solid and productive hard worker. Expect him to be selected early in the second round.
David Lee

A good, solid pick for the Magic and one we pegged this morning -- albeit three picks later. He can stretch defenses with his perimeter skills, but he's really a hustle guy who will attack the boards and do all the dirty things that you love in a reserve.

analysis.text: Markota is a very athletic small forward.  Excellent leaper (he owns a 36-inch vertical). A solid shooter.  Very aggressive on the offensive end of the floor.  He's always looking for his shot. Good rebounder. Has improved his body dramatically over the past two years.

Short arms mean that he actually plays smaller than he is.  Has had major issues with maturity (he's flaky, a party animal) in the past, though many of those seem to have been solved the past year.  Scouts say that he's not a good defender. Still needs to develop a mid-range game.

Plays for Cibona in Croatia.  Averaged 7.7 ppg and 5.1 rpg in 20 mpg in the Eurolege this season. Markota, who two years ago entered the draft under the name Damir Omerhodzic,  didn't impress many teams during workouts in the summer of 2004, and rumors about off-the-court problems hurt his stock to the point that he didn't even consider the 2005 draft.  However, after a breakout performance in the European Under 20 Championships in Russia, scouts are starting to take notice again.  Markota averaged 18.5 ppg and 11 rpg, was hitting his jumper and was very aggressive on both ends of the floor.
Second round

If he can prove to scouts that he's matured and that he can hit his shot consistently in the pros, he'll get some serious interest from scouts in the late first round. However, right now he's a solid second rounder.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Markota is not a stranger to the draft, having declared in 2004 before pulling his name out. The big question with him is what his NBA skill is. There isn't anything very special about his game. He is limited athletically, especially with his lateral movement. He is a strong, but short-armed, skilled power forward.

Markota is versatile, plays hard and is a very tough kid. He scores most of his points by overpowering post players on the block and is a solid shooter with decent range. His face-up game is decent. Markota is a smart player, good in the low post and versatile enough to be able to use his left and right hand with jump hooks to either shoulder.

However, Markota has several issues that could hinder his draft status. His lack of length (short arms) and inability to defend are on-court issues. He also has had some off-court issues in the past with his maturity and nightlife.

He is a solid player but lacks an outstanding pro skill. He does not appear to have a big NBA upside. Some team could draft him in the second round, hold his rights and see what happens.
Another nice, late-round international steal for the Spurs. Markota has size, can shoot it and is putting up good numbers in Croatia. He'll stay in Europe but he could be an NBA player down the road.

Eliyahu does just about everything well. He has NBA 3-point  range, has great 
moves in the paint, can handle the ball and moves his  feet well on the 
defensive end. He's a combo forward who can rebound, shoot the three and handle the basketball.   Has long arms and good athletic ability.

Scouts aren't sure exactly what position he'll play in the pros. Needs to get stronger to play the four.  Needs to improve his perimeter game to play the three. The competition he plays against isn't stellar.  A mandatory commitment to the Israeli army may delay his ability to play in the NBA anytime soon.

Plays for Galil Elyon Golan in Israel. Eliyahu had a breakout game at the Reebok Eurocamp in Treviso in May of 2005.  He continued to impress scouts with two solid tournament performances this summer.  Eliyahu averaged 18.6 ppg and 6.3 rpg at the European Under 20 Championships in Russia.
Second round to undrafted
The hope of Israel.  He's a potential first-round pick if he continues to progress.  However, right now he's planted firmly in the second round.

Orlando traded this pick to the Rockets. He'll stay in Israel and play for the top team there, Maccabi, for another couple of years. He's a long-term prospect, but he has good athleticism, plays hard and is always around the ball. Check back in two years.

analysis.text: An amazing athlete with a great NBA body.  Long arms. He can jump out of the gym and has the strength to post up.  Great rebounder for a two guard. Very tough.  Plays physical.  Pretty good off the dribble.  Explodes to the basket. Excellent defender.

He's a shaky shooter.  Adams launches a lot of 3s, but they don't really go in all that often.  His shot selection can be shaky, especially when he settles for shooting 3s.  He's got to attack the basket more and retire that 3-point jumper. Not a good ball handler.  Undersized for his position.
Second round to undrafted

Some scouts love Adams, but most aren't that high on his NBA prospects. He's an amazing physical specimen, but his basketball IQ seems low. The comparisons to Andre Iguodala are ridiculous. Both are great athletes, but Iguodala has a great feel for the game. Adams doesn't. He's probably a second-round pick.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Adams entered the draft last year but pulled out and went back to Arizona. He has an NBA body and athleticism and is a very explosive player with big-time hops. He was one of the most exciting players in college basketball this past season. He is a very good defender with very quick feet and good hands. He is a little undersized to play the two-guard, but with his strong body and toughness, he might be able to do it. With long arms and leaping ability, Adams is a very good rebounder for an off-guard.

However, Adams is lacking a true NBA skill. He is a poor shooter and has a poor shot selection. He is much more effective attacking the rim. He is pretty good off the dribble and would be better as a more consistent slasher and driver. He also has had some issues off the court which may come back to haunt him in the draft. While it might be more a matter of maturity than of him being a bad kid, at this time of year any off-court problems can affect his draft status.

Adams is similar to Tony Allen of the Celtics. He is a smaller wing player who is strong and athletic. His ability to defend, run the court and take the ball to the rim will attract teams in the second round.

Shooting isn't his forte, but Adams defends his man very well.

Nice pickup for the Nets. They thought about taking Adams with the No. 23 pick.  He's an elite athlete and very tough. Doesn't have much of a perimeter game but will add some toughness to their perimeter game.

One of the best shooters in the draft. Deep range on his jumper. Great pick- and-pop guy. Great size for his position.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: Outstanding long-range shooter. Has NBA 3-point range. Can shoot it off the catch and also coming off screens. Reads and uses screens effectively and knows when to fade or curl off the screen. Will be a very good screen-and-space guy because of his ability to shoot it off the catch.

Is clever enough to get is own shot by a very effective square-up jab series. Excellent shot fake, one dribble, shot player. Basketball IQ is very good and knows how to get space to get his shot off. He is always shot-ready off the catch.

Deceptive speed and quickness. Understands the game and knows how to compensate for his lack of quickness. Will be able to defend on the perimeter, as he is long enough and mentally tough enough to space people he is guarding.

Will stick his nose in there and rebound. Not a great athlete but a strong-willed kid who finds a way to get it done. Has a good feel for where the ball is coming off the glass and can run down loose balls.

Not a blow-by player off the dribble and needs improvement taking the ball all the way to the rim to finish. If he can improve in that area it will help him in getting to the line, where he is an outstanding free-throw shooter.

Low-maintenance, high-character kid who has a great work ethic. Wants to get better and will put in the necessary hours to do so. Always a place for a kid like this.
The Rockets love tall guys who can stretch the defense with their 3-point shooting. He doesn't do much else, but he really can shoot it.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Hollins is a perfect example of an underachiever. He had all the potential in the world when he arrived at UCLA as a freshman. He has size, length and can run. But he was labeled soft by most coaches and scouts, and he never showed up when the team really needed him.

He has good hands and scores most of his points on offensive put-backs and by running the floor. He had a very productive NCAA Tournament, helping lead UCLA to the championship game. But he doesn't have much of a face-up game or much range on his jump shot. Hollins isn't a big fan of contact or fighting for position in the post.

He has potential to be a pro if he has time to develop, but it will take a lot of work. He's really a major project for a team to invest in, reminiscent a bit of Loren Woods of the Toronto Raptors. If Hollins gets drafted at all, he will go late in the second round.

The Bobcats were hoping that David Noel would be here but are happy with Hollins. He's long and athletic and he can block shots. He's been an underachiever at UCLA, but if he ever gets it, he could be good.

Veremeenko slowly gained momentum this season after an impressive performance last summer at the Reebok Eurocamp.  Veremeenko has added enough muscle to defend the four position. On offense, he's a match-up problem. He has excellent perimeter skills and is a fundamentally sound, good, but not great, athlete.  Excellent basketball IQ.  Experienced.

For years, Veremeenko was the classic European tweener. He wasn't quite big enough or strong enough to play the four, and his feet weren't quick enough to guard threes.  However, scouts' opinions are changing as they believe Veremeenko has added the muscle to play the four.
Plays for Dynamo St. Petersburg.  Averaged 11.8 ppg and 6.2 rpg while shooting 60 percent from the field.  Only shot 32 percent from three.
Second round to undrafted

Veremeenko doesn't have one skill or physical attribute that makes him a top prospect, but he has a great feel for the game. He doesn't do anything to turn your head when he's on the court, but at the end of the game, he'll have filled the stat sheet and led his team to victory. Today, he's a second rounder. He'll likely stay there. But he could be a bargain for whoever drafts him.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Veremeenko came on the scene last year and is one of the more underrated Europeans in this year's draft. There has been a lot of talk about Damir Markota when teams should be talking about Veremeenko. He has been one of the more talented young players in Russia the past two years.

Veremeenko is very tough, has good size and can score. He is tough enough to rebound on both ends of the floor and do whatever it takes to win. He is a versatile player for whom you don't need to run plays to help your team win. He does a variety of things on both the offensive and defensive ends to be effective.

He has a variety of moves he uses in the post, as well as a nice 15- to 17-foot jump shot. He is a post player you can go to on the block, or you can pull him away from the basket and run pick-and-pops for him. There is some doubt about his athletic ability, though, and that will hurt his chances of sneaking into the late first round. NBA teams may be looking more to draft in the second round and hold his rights while he spends more time in Europe.
Veremeenko is an interesting pick. He's a bit of a tweener, but he's had some success in Russia. He's probably staying overseas for a few more years.
Very good shooter.  Deep range.  Good athlete.  Has a knack for scoring the ball.

He's very undersized for his position and doesn't have the versatility to be anything more than a bench gunner.  He's a good, but not great perimeter shooter when he has to put the ball on the floor.  Not a great ball handler.

Ray has had an excellent season -- but his NBA upside is questionable because of his size.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: Excellent shooter with NBA 3-point range. Very good shooter off the catch and has the speed to get out in transition and spot up for 3-point shots.

Will be very good at coming off screens, as he has a knack for knowing whether to curl or fade off the screen. Has a very quick release after he catches it off the screen. Not as effective shooting it off the dribble. Has a jump-shooter mentality and will need to improve his ability to take it to the rim and finish.

Not a player who is going to put it on the floor and make plays for others, as he is more about putting it on the floor to create a shot for himself. His mid-range jumper is good off the dribble but is still better off the catch.

Needs to continue to get stronger and become a more physical player. His lack of strength -- not lack of effort -- makes him a liability on defense and on the boards. Has the speed, quickness and effort to defend but gets taken advantage of at times by stronger, more physical players.

A gym rat. Been known to be in the gym every day shooting up to 1,000 shots. Has a big-time love for the game and really wants to work to get better. High character, low maintenance.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: Very good shooter for his size. Big-time shooter off the catch, and you better find him when he is trailing in transition, because he will knock down NBA-range jump shots off the catch. A very good high-post player who will be very effective in the two-man game as a dangerous screen-and-pop shooter.

Not nearly as effective as a post-up player. Is strong and physical enough down low but is not nearly as good finishing inside as he is facing, catching and shooting. However, he is an excellent passer out of the low-post area and usually makes the right plays.

Average rebounder and is going to rebound only in his immediate area, as he lacks the athletic ability to go and get rebounds. Not a shot blocker but will alter shots because of his size. Has a tough time defending the two-man game. Not real good at showing and getting back to his man. Just not quick enough.

High-quality high-post system player who can rally shoot it. There is always a place for a player of his size who can space and shoot like he can. Could he be a Bill Laimbeer type?

Stinson is a scoring point guard with great size who likes to take the ball to the basket.  He's got a great basketball IQ and is an excellent passer.  He's very strong and likes to take smaller guards down in the paint.  When he gets to the rim, he's a great finisher.  Great body.

The big thing holding him back is his jump shot. While his mid-range jumper is solid, he's not much of a long-range threat from 3. Shaky defender. Scouts wonder whether he's really a point guard or a shooting guard at the next level.  Even we can't make up our minds.  His age isn't a huge issue, but he's older than most of the juniors in the NCAA.  Some off-the-court attitude issues also are bothering teams.

Stinson announced that he's declaring for the 2006 NBA Draft and hired an agent, ending college eligibility.

Wingspan: 6-5

Second round

Stinson's had a stellar season for Iowa State. His assists were up. His turnovers were down. And his shot was falling. His solid play at the Orlando predraft camp should help him.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: Stinson, a three-year starter in the same backcourt with Will Blalock, is an extremely strong guard with a rock-solid body. He has decent speed but is not overly quick.

Stinson has an aggressive offensive mentality. He loves to overpower weaker perimeter players by taking them into the paint. He is both a scorer (19.4 points per game) and a distributor (5.5 assists), but he still has trouble with decision-making, as his 3.4 turnovers per game indicate. Stinson is not a true point guard, and that's a major question mark with NBA teams. His ball-handling abilities are suspect, and he has a tough time against pressure.

He has an excellent mid-range game with a wonderful floater in the lane, but he is not a very good shooter from distance. Stinson had good stats in college, but he had many big games against weaker opponents and tended to struggle against stronger teams that could match his strength with a strong and athletic guard. He sometimes puts his head down and tries to overpower them and gets frustrated.

Defensively, Iowa State played exclusively zone to protect Stinson, and he is going to have major problems guarding at the next level. He is a poor on-the-ball defender, and quicker guards will blow by him from the top or wings.

He was a tough guy to play with in college. He missed a lot of practice time and has some issues with temper and composure that date all the way back to high school. It is not a surprise to those that know him that his team underachieved and his coach got fired.

Stinson has many flaws in his game that have worried NBA scouts. In addition the NBA workouts have exposed his inability to shoot and defend one-on-one. Combine these physical problems with his character issues and practice habits, and you know why this kid is slipping every day.

Scouts Inc. Evaluation: A very versatile and athletic wing player, Noel was an important contributor to North Carolina's 2005 National Championship team and averaged 13 points and 7 rebounds for the UNC in the 2005-06 season. He has good size, is very strong and plays very hard.

Noel has good ability to rebound and post-up from the small forward spot. He can score on mid-range shots and is good coming off down-screens. However, he has proven to be an inconsistent shooter. He shot 42.4 percent last season from the college 3-point line but has been only a 55-60 percent free-throw shooter in his career. For someone who has the ability get to the free-throw line, he desperately needs to improve his shooting.

Noel doesn't have an NBA skill which separates him from other players. He has potential to make it, because he is very tough, versatile and scores in different ways. But he needs to improve his shooting consistency and ball handling. He'll be either a late second-round pick or go undrafted.
Love this pick for the Bucks. Noel ranked as the best athlete in the draft and is still developing as a basketball player. Could become a Bobby Simmons-type player down the road.
A big-time scorer with great speed.  Thrives penetrating to the basket.  Great first step. Excellent finisher. Has a solid body.  Pretty strong.

Is he really a point guard? Averaged just 3.3 assists with 3.1 turnovers this season.  Looks for his shot first, pass second.  Doesn't show much of an inclination to defend.  Three-point shooting declined this year.

Washington announced on April 25 that he was declaring for the 2006 NBA Draft. From the sounds of things, he's staying in the draft no matter what.

Wingspan: 6-4

Standing reach: 8-0

Maximum vertical jump: 37.5 inches
Second round

Washington's decision to stay in the draft could be a very bad idea. While Washington has the size, speed and athleticism to be an excellent NBA prospect, his production actually decreased from his freshman year. His numbers were down across the board this year. However, an excellent performance at the Orlando predraft camp has helped his stock. A small minority of scouts say they think Washington will be a better pro than college player, and they like the idea of Washington as a scoring combo guard coming off the bench. Right now he looks like a mid- to late second-round pick. However, it takes only one team to fall in love with a player (see the Blazers two years ago with Sebastian Telfair), so you never know.

Scouts Inc. evaluation: Coming out of high school two years ago, Washington was the second-best point guard in the country behind Telfair. He has had a nice career at Memphis, and he is making a poor decision coming out for this year's draft.

Washington has the ability to create some offense for himself, but his lack of explosiveness will make it very difficult for him to get into the lane in the NBA or to defend opposing point guards. His lack of point-guard skills was evident in his averaging only 3 assists per game last season, despite all of the athletic weapons he had to play with at Memphis. He is a shoot-first point guard who turned the ball over 3 times per game, something that can be attributed to his lack of length. He also has struggled shooting the ball at times, which doesn't help his hopes of getting drafted in the first round.

Given all of the questions about his ability to make the transition, staying in the draft is a big mistake. He needs to go back to school and show people he can run a team, cut down on his turnovers and improve his shooting. He never will become an explosive player, but he can improve on some attributes that can make him a serviceable point guard in the NBA.
